atom:entry.atom:title: OpenID4VP: X.509 chain validation accepts a forged certificate that reuses a trusted anchor's Subject DN without verifying its signature
atom:entry.atom:summary:
Severity: HIGH / CVSS 7.5 (v3.1)
Summary: ## Summary `ChainBuilder` (the private RFC 5280 validator behind `TrustEvaluator` and the public credential-parsing API) terminated chain building on **Subject Distinguished Name string equality** rather than on cryptographic closure to a trust anchor. A certificate whose Subject DN string matched a trusted anchor's Subject DN was accepted as the chain terminus **with no signature verification** against the anchor's public key. An attacker who mints a self-signed certificate and copies a trusted anchor's Subject DN string onto it can therefore have that certificate - and any credential signed with its private key - accepted as issued under a trusted authority. ## Impact A relying party using `@openeudi/openid4vp` to verify OpenID4VP presentations (mdoc / SD-JWT VC) could be induced to accept a **forged credential as genuine**, defeating the trust-anchor model.
